RagShortTexts: The Île de la Cité on the Seine held French royal majesty, flanked by Sorbonne scholars in.

Variants.Content: Encircled by the Seine, the Île de la Cité anchors Capetian royal power, home to Notre-Dame and the jewel-box Sainte-Chapelle. On the Left Bank, the Collège de Sorbonne (founded 1257 by Robert de Sorbon) draws masters like Thomas Aquinas, establishing the Latin Quarter as Western Europe's intellectual capital.

Students from four nations—French, Picard, Norman, and English—sit on straw-covered floors debating Aristotelian dialectic. Vellum parchment dressers and illuminated book copyists drive a booming trade.

Bridges over the Seine are crowded with two-story houses and cobblers' stalls. Carting country butter and cider into the central market at Les Halles means paying gate tolls, but Paris silver coin never depreciates.
